reading: Two facing rectangles; the background strip between them (across their shared rows or columns) is filled with 8, inset by one cell at each end of the overlap.

new_rows.name: inner_between
new_rows.datalog:
bgc(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), !cell(Y, X, C).
hl(Y, X) :- bgc(Y, X), cell(Y, X1, C), X1 < X.
hr(Y, X) :- bgc(Y, X), cell(Y, X1, C), X1 > X.
hb(Y, X) :- hl(Y, X), hr(Y, X).
vu(Y, X) :- bgc(Y, X), cell(Y1, X, C), Y1 < Y.
vd(Y, X) :- bgc(Y, X), cell(Y1, X, C), Y1 > Y.
vb(Y, X) :- vu(Y, X), vd(Y, X).
inner_between(Y, X) :- hb(Y, X), Y1 = Y - 1, hb(Y1, X), Y2 = Y + 1, hb(Y2, X).
inner_between(Y, X) :- vb(Y, X), X1 = X - 1, vb(Y, X1), X2 = X + 1, vb(Y, X2).

why: every filled cell is background lying between the two rectangles and not on the first/last line of their overlap; colour is always 8

reading: Diamond outlines of colour 2 shrink by one ring (concentric), diamond outlines of colour 5 grow by one ring; shapes of other colours (8, 9) stay. Clipped at the grid edge.

slots.subject: each diamond outline object of colour 2 or 5
slots.delta: colour 2 -> radius-1 (radius 1 becomes a single centre cell), colour 5 -> radius+1

why: each 2/5 object in the output is the input object's diamond with the same centre and radius changed by one (one pair-0 corner piece is off by a column)

reading: Every closed loop of 1s gets a one-cell halo: background cells touching it (8-neighbour) on the outside become 2, those on the inside become 3. Open (non-enclosing) shapes stay unchanged.

slots.subject: 1-objects that enclose background
slots.outer: outside bg cells 8-adjacent to the loop -> 2
slots.inner: enclosed bg cells 8-adjacent to the loop -> 3

why: only loops that enclose a hole are decorated; open shapes untouched

reading: The grid is a 4x6 array of 3x3 glyphs; one glyph is drawn in 8. Every glyph with the same shape becomes 8, and every glyph lying between two 8-glyphs in the same glyph-row or glyph-column becomes 7.

slots.cells: 3x3 glyph slots separated by blank rows/cols
slots.match: glyphs identical in shape to the key -> recoloured 8
slots.between: glyphs strictly between two 8-glyphs on a glyph-row or glyph-column -> recoloured 7

why: on all pairs the 8s are exactly the key-shaped glyphs and the 7s exactly the glyphs between two of them

reading: Two blocks face each other across the grid; each grows toward the other over half the gap, as a full-width band (its span widened by one on each side), leaving one background line in the middle when the gap is odd.

slots.subject: the two coloured blocks
slots.extent: half the gap each (floor), band spans block rows/cols plus one each side

why: each half of the gap is filled with the colour of the nearer block; middle line stays background when the gap length is odd

reading: A shape is split by an empty row or column through its middle; that whole grid row or column is filled with 3.

new_rows.name: gap_line
new_rows.datalog:
filled_row(Y) :- cell(Y, X, C).
filled_col(X) :- cell(Y, X, C).
gap_row(Y) :- px(Y, X, C), !filled_row(Y), cell(Y1, X1, C1), Y1 < Y, cell(Y2, X2, C2), Y2 > Y.
gap_col(X) :- px(Y, X, C), !filled_col(X), cell(Y1, X1, C1), X1 < X, cell(Y2, X2, C2), X2 > X.
gap_line(Y, X) :- gap_row(Y), px(Y, X, C).
gap_line(Y, X) :- gap_col(X), px(Y, X, C).

why: the filled line is the one empty row/column with shape cells on both sides; colour is always 3

reading: A dotted rectangular frame becomes a solid outline with a cleared interior; the small dotted pieces lying outside it are removed and placed inside the frame as solid blocks (their boxes filled), packed side by side.

slots.container: the dotted frame object (made solid, interior set to background)
slots.pieces: dotted multi-cell pieces outside the frame, each becoming a filled box of its colour
slots.placement: packed inside the frame interior with a one-cell margin
slots.rest: original piece locations restored to the background dot pattern

why: output has exactly the pieces' filled boxes inside the solid frame and none outside
invariants: background dot lattice outside the frame unchanged

reading: A 1 at the top drops down its column; if it lands in a watertight cup of 2s, the cup's interior is filled with 1, otherwise (outside the cup or the cup leaks) the whole bottom row becomes 1. The marker is removed.

slots.outcome_closed: cup interior between the walls filled with 1

why: cup filled exactly when the marker column is inside a cup with closed bottom; else bottom row

reading: Each 9 square of side s gets a 3 border of thickness s/2 around it and a 1 beam of its width running down from below the border to the bottom edge; 9 over 3 over 1.

slots.subject: each 9 square
slots.beam: colour 1, square's columns, from below the halo to the bottom border

why: halo thickness equals half the square side on every pair; beams stop only at the bottom border and are covered by halos

reading: Every two 1 cells on the same row or column are joined by a line of 8 over the background between them.
why: every 8 cell is background between two 1s on one row or column; colour is 8
